why: heap-stage5 section 15: a call of an imported function is a transition of the whole heap world; the identity certificate is the same transitions in the same order. usedOnce names the result before using it once (proved); usedTwice reads two fields of the returned reference, named or inline, in the world the call returned (proved); writtenBack writes the result into a field of the argument and returns the field instead of the result (unproved: the transition may write every object and leaves no frame, so the argument's cell after it is unknown, as an accessor the callee installs would make it; lane B's real module keeps the field, PASS-bounded); calledTwice calls twice for once (unproved: the environment may answer the second call otherwise; the real module answers both alike, PASS-bounded); passedOn and passedLocal pass the result on to another transition and to a function of this file (proved); passedSwapped passes it on in the other argument of a transition that is not symmetric (unproved, WITNESS); passedRef reads the quantity of a returned reference before the save instead of after (unproved, WITNESS: the save writes it). The operands are evaluated in order, then the transition: readFirst passes the quantity read before bump in the parent and after it in the candidate (unproved, WITNESS); readFirstNamed names the quantity before the call, the same order (proved). The right operand of && runs only when the left is true: guarded calls bump whatever c holds in the candidate (unproved, WITNESS); guardedIf returns early instead, the same transitions (proved).
